source_warnings: Huang, Knight and Naprienko 2025 (arXiv:2507.21404v2, artifact e766c8aa4f94287672b2b1bacab2480a41ec7c806ecbaf5e2d1bf8773781310f, Abstract) audit LIT-PCBA and report extensive analogue and 2D-identical-compound leakage between its splits: 323 active training-validation analogue pairs at ECFP4 Tanimoto at or above 0.6 in ALDH1 alone and 2491 2D-identical inactives shared between training and validation across targets. They conclude that a parameter-free memorisation baseline matches or exceeds published deep-learning and 3D-similarity results, that nearly all published LIT-PCBA results are undermined, that zero-shot evaluations are also affected, and that the benchmark does not measure recovery of novel chemotypes. That bears on this value.

The actives-to-inactives ratio of LIT-PCBA is in dispute between the sources: the official page (artifact a2203612b553236d7f01da5573389d439d2f7aa0436080412f27da882e086e5e, data content table) gives 7761 actives and 382674 unique inactives for the 15 target sets, while Shen et al. 2025 (artifact 11a4cee97057d9e72f9393024d22fdd169e3134f493367eee2f7869facf9ccf8, Methods 'Datasets') give 10030 confirmed actives and 2798737 confirmed inactives. Neither source reconciles the other. NEF1% is defined as a correction for that ratio, so the normalised values rest on a count the sources disagree about.
